newsitem.title: UK: Delay would harm Eurofighter export prospects -UK.
newsitem.headline: Delay would harm Eurofighter export prospects -UK.

text.p: British defence secretary Michael Portillo warned on Monday that the export prospects of the four-nation Eurofighter would be endangered by further delay in getting the go-ahead for its production.
"If it is to have good export prospects, the aircraft needs to be produced without further delay," Portillo said in a parliamentary debate on Britain's defence spending.
"If collaborative projects are to offer European nations a competitive alternative to buying American we need to improve markedly on our performance to date," Portillo added.

Portillo was speaking on the day after the chairman of the German parliament's defence committee told BBC television his country would be hard pushed to afford the Eurofighter given the need to trim public spending.

"We are in a difficult financial situation in Germany so from this point of view we perhaps could not afford it," Klaus Rose said. "But I think as we need it from the military point of view and as it is a quadrilateral cooperation, we have to."
The Eurofighter is due to be built by a consortium linking British Aerospace Plc, Germany's Daimler Benz, unit Dasa, Alenia SpA of Italy and Spain's CASA.
